family: National forest boundary, consolidation, transfer, name and administrative-site orders (X1 type national_forest_boundary)

mechanisms.description: A later executive order revoked or rescinded the member in full. Forty-eight members are revoked in full by forty-three later members of this same family whose held texts name them by number and date.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The date of the revoking order (fixed per branch).

mechanisms.description: The order withdrew lands 'until' a stated date in aid of pending legislation and said the lands would then become subject to disposal without further order.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The stated date in the order (or in a held extension order), fixed per branch.

mechanisms.description: An order whose only operative content is to revoke, rescind or abolish another order (or a site reserved by it), and at most to restore or open the released land to entry under the general land laws, is executed on issue; its effect is evidence for the other order's lifecycle.

An order whose only operative content is to amend, correct or extend a cited executive order or proclamation is executed on issue; its content becomes part of the amended instrument, whose lifecycle it informs.

An order that excludes described land from a national forest under the 1897 Act and at most restores or opens that land to the public-land laws (including preference periods and opening schedules) performs a single act: the land leaves the reservation on the order and is thereafter governed by the general land laws, not by the order.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Order date (spent on issue); a stated opening schedule runs a few weeks or months after it, which the gap notes.

mechanisms.description: Administrative-site, classification, resurvey and pending-legislation withdrawals made under the Pickett Act have no built-in end and remain in force until revoked by the President or Congress; FLPMA (1976) repealed the authority but saved existing withdrawals. Persistence on 2026-10-14 still needs a current land record.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: None: an end needs a revocation (later executive order or public land order) or statute reaching the land.

mechanisms.description: Orders that create a forest from parts of others, transfer land between forests, merge one forest into another, add land, rename a forest or redraw its boundaries operate on the forest's continuing designation. Whether such an order is spent on issue (merged into the forest's establishing instrument) or persists as long as the designation does is an owner question; under either reading NFMA (1976) bars return of land still reserved as national forest to the public domain except by Act of Congress.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: None until the owner decides; the Forest Service chronological record would date later consolidations and renamings forest by forest.

sources.title: General Withdrawal Act (Pickett Act)
sources.pin: and such withdrawals or reservations shall remain in force until revoked by him or by an Act of Congress
sources.establishes: A withdrawal made under the Act, though called temporary, remains in force until the President or Congress revokes it, so an administrative-site or classification withdrawal has no built-in end (read on the web 2026-11-05, not held; the amendment at 37 Stat. 497 was not read).

sources.establishes: Withdrawals and reservations in effect on October 21, 1976 remain in full force until modified under FLPMA or other law, so FLPMA's repeal of the withdrawal statutes did not end any member.

sources.citation: Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976, Pub. L. 94-579, sec. 704(a), 90 Stat. 2743, 2792
sources.title: FLPMA repeal of withdrawal laws
sources.establishes: Effective October 21, 1976 FLPMA repealed the President's forest-reservation authority (Act of Mar. 3, 1891, sec. 24, 26 Stat. 1103, 16 U.S.C. 471) and the Pickett Act (36 Stat. 847); a repeal of authority, which under the owner's rule is not an end of orders already made.

sources.citation: National Forest Management Act of 1976, Pub. L. 94-588, sec. 9, 90 Stat. 2949, 2957, amending sec. 11(a) of the Forest and Rangeland Renewable Resources Planning Act of 1974 (16 U.S.C. 1609(a))
sources.title: National Forest System; no return of reserved forest land to the public domain except by Act of Congress
sources.pin: no land now or hereafter reserved or withdrawn from the public domain as national forests
sources.establishes: From October 22, 1976, land reserved or withdrawn from the public domain as national forest under the Act of March 3, 1891 or acts supplementary to it may be returned to the public domain only by Act of Congress; it protects land still in a forest in 1976 but says nothing about whether a particular order's land was still in a forest then (read on the web 2026-11-05, not held).

sources.citation: Act of March 4, 1907, ch. 2907, 34 Stat. 1256, 1271 (Agricultural Appropriation Act for fiscal year 1908, proviso; 16 U.S.C. 471 note)
sources.title: Bar on new national forests or additions in six western states except by Act of Congress
sources.pin: nor shall any additions be made to one heretofore created
sources.establishes: After March 4, 1907 no forest could be created or enlarged by the President in Oregon, Washington, Idaho, Montana, Colorado or Wyoming; it bears on the validity of additions there, not on when any member ended (read on the web 2026-11-05, not held).

procedure.description: Revokes, rescinds or abolishes another order or a site it reserved, and at most restores or opens the released land to entry; no new reservation follows the revocation.

not.text_regex: (revoked|rescinded|vacated|abolished)\b.{0,1500}?(rewithdrawn|re-withdrawn|(hereby|be|are) (temporarily )?withdrawn|(?<!been )(?<!heretofore )reserved (for|as) (?!forest)|be reserved|townsite|town site|town-site|transferred to|made a part of|added to|in aid of|(?<!or )pending (legislation|classification)|national forest is hereby|shall be known|(restored|returned) to (the )?[\w' ]{0,30}National Forest|remain (a )?part of|(become|be) a part of|declared to be (a )?part)
(hereby|be|are) (temporarily )?withdrawn from settlement|hereby (reserved|set apart)|be reserved for|is hereby established

lead.basis: The order's only command revokes another order (with at most a restoration or opening of the released land), which it performed on issue; whether the revoked order ended is recorded on that order.

gaps: Where the order also sets an opening schedule (for example 91 days for ex-service men from the 63d day), the last scheduled step falls after the order date; the order date is the spent-on-issue date under the owner's rule, not the date the schedule finished.

procedure.description: Amends, corrects or extends a cited executive order or proclamation and does nothing else (no new withdrawal, exclusion or addition of its own).

not.text_regex: Indian|natives|townsite|town site|transferred to|transfer of|made a part of|shall be known|hereafter (be )?known|military|naval|enlarg|addition of|(hereby|be|are) (temporarily )?withdrawn from settlement|be reserved for|hereby (reserved|set apart)|boundary between|remain (a )?part of|declared to be|lands so situated

lead.basis: The order's only command amends, corrects or extends another instrument, which it performed on issue; its content is evidence for the amended instrument's lifecycle.

gaps: An extension is executed on issue under the owner's rule; the extended instrument carries the later end date.

procedure.description: Excludes described land from a forest (or opens to entry land an earlier order or proclamation excluded) and at most restores or opens it to the general land laws (with or without a preference or opening schedule, a state school-land preference, or a disposal direction under a general statute); no addition, transfer, townsite, Indian, military, classification or other reservation of the land.

not.text_regex: townsite|town site|town-site|Indian|natives|military|naval|War Department|transferred to|transfer of|made a part of|administered as (a )?part|constitut\w* (a |the )?(part|portion)|portions? of the [A-Z][a-z]+ National|added to|in addition to|addition of|by (adding|including)|to include|(be|is|are|hereby)\s*,?\s*(hereby\s*)?enlarged|enlarged by|(?<!were )(?<!lands )(?<!been )withdrawn (pending|in aid|from settlement)|(?<!were )(?<!lands )(?<!been )withdrawn for (?!forestry|coal)|temporarily withdrawn|(?<!or )pending (legislation|classification|determination|resurvey|exchange)|in aid of|(?<!were )(?<!been )(?<!heretofore )reserved (for|as) (?!forestry)|be reserved|terminal reserve|railroad (purposes|terminal|reserve)|power site|reservoir|water supply|exchange|school (reservation|site|purpose)|shall be known|hereafter (be )?known|interchange|merge|remain (a )?part of|declared to be|(are|is|be),? (hereby,? )?(temporarily )?withdrawn|(?<!coal )for classification

lead.basis: Under the 1897 Act (30 Stat. 36) the order reduced the forest's area by excluding the described land, or opened to entry land already excluded; that single act took effect on the order, after which the land was governed by the general public-land laws rather than by the order.

gaps: Where the order fixes a later opening date or preference period, the last scheduled step falls after the order date; the order date is the spent-on-issue date.
A later proclamation or order that re-added the same land to a forest would be a new reservation, not a revival of this order; it does not change this lead.

procedure.description: Withdraws land for a ranger station, administrative site, lookout, dock or boathouse site, road material or similar Forest Service use (not revoked by a held member order).

when.any_regex: ranger station|ranger-station|administrative site|administrative-site|administration site|lookout|dock site|boathouse|right of way|right-of-way|road (construction|material)|for use (by|of) the Forest Service

lead.basis: A Pickett Act withdrawal stays in force until revoked by the President or Congress and survived FLPMA's repeal of the authority; no held instrument revokes this one, and no current land record has been read.

gaps: A search of public land orders (Federal Register 1942-) and of the BLM land-status record (Mineral and Land Records System, serial register) for a revocation of this withdrawal; absent a revocation, a current record showing the withdrawal open would support a yes.

procedure.description: Withdraws or reserves land for classification, resurvey, exchange, or in aid of legislation (often to add it to a forest), without a stated end date.

when.any_regex: pending (the )?(legislation|classification|resurvey|determination|exchange|inclusion|selection)|in aid of (the )?(pending )?legislation|for classification|pending resurvey|withdrawn for|aid of legislation

not.text_regex: included in and made a part of|hereby (added to|included in) the

lead.basis: The withdrawal has no stated end; it ended only if revoked, or if a later statute or proclamation by its terms disposed of the land, and no held instrument shows either.

gaps: The later instrument for the same land: the Act of Congress or proclamation that added it to a forest (Forest Service chronological record lists these), or a revoking executive order or public land order.

procedure.description: Creates or continues a reservation for another purpose: water-supply protection for a military post, Indian or native use, townsite, military, railroad terminal, school, hot springs, or excluded land so reserved.

when.any_regex: water supply|Indian|natives|townsite|town site|town-site|military|naval|War Department|railroad|terminal|school|hot springs|medicinal springs

lead.basis: The order makes a continuing reservation of land for a purpose other than a forest boundary change; its end depends on later instruments for that land, none held.

gaps: Later instruments for the reserved land (revocation, transfer to the Indian reservation's trust status, townsite disposal, military transfer); members of this kind may also fall under the Indian, military-reservation or land-withdrawal family doctrines.

procedure.description: Creates a forest from parts of others, transfers land between forests, merges forests, adds land, renames a forest, or redraws its boundary (including mixed orders that also exclude land).

lead.basis: The order fixes the continuing designation or boundary of a national forest; whether it is spent on issue (merged into the forest's establishing instrument) or persists with the designation is undecided, and no current Forest Service record has been read.

gaps: Owner decision on whether a boundary, transfer, consolidation or name order is spent on issue as an amendment of the forest's establishing instrument.

Under the persistence reading: the Forest Service chronological record (later consolidation or renaming of the named forest) and the current Land Areas Report (the forest or name still exists on 2026-10-14).

procedure.description: Anything else.

lead.basis: The held text matched no branch; the order must be read individually.

gaps: Individual reading of the order text.

undecidable.reason: Forest creation, transfer, consolidation, addition, renaming and boundary-redescription orders: undecided pending the owner's choice between the spent-on-issue (merger) reading and the persistence reading, and under the latter pending the Forest Service chronological record and Land Areas Report.
Administrative-site and similar Forest Service withdrawals not revoked by a held order: need a public land order search or BLM land-status record.
Classification, resurvey, exchange and pending-legislation withdrawals without a stated end: need the later Act, proclamation or revocation for the land.
Reservations for other purposes (Indian, townsite, military, water supply, school): need later instruments for the land; may belong to other family doctrines.
